Triage: `needs-user-decision` + `domain:services` + type **Feature** — human floor twice over (new capability class; multi-week programme needing appetite). `target:v18` kept as filed: this is v18 planning scope, not a current-release blocker. The five design decisions in the body are genuine product semantics (mirror-vs-adopt, association timing, unmatched pool, mailbox topology, privacy posture) — none is triage-adjudicable.

## Four-axis card face

1. **Platform long-term coherence**: the three-layer split (connector / sync service / association seam) follows the existing `packages/connectors/` convention, and the seam keeps "what is a contact" out of the platform — contract-first, enterprise extends rather than forks. The `sys_email` outbound precedent gives the inbound mirror (`sys_mail_message`) a shape that already exists.
2. **Measured business pull**: strongest axis — a live bank-CRM RFI where this was the single largest risk (~60 person-days quoted), plus the marketplace flagship (HotCRM) failing the first thing every CRM evaluator tries. Comparable open CRMs all ship inbound mail free; the open-core placement argument is concrete, not speculative.
3. **AI-agent error-resistance**: platform-owned normalized objects + one closed extension point ("which record(s) do these participants belong to?") is structurally harder to misuse than per-app bespoke IMAP ingest; the privacy posture must be a declarable closed policy (folder allowlist / known-contact / per-message share), not runtime tolerance.
4. **Startup scope discipline**: the counterweight — 2 connectors + 2 services + a seam is the largest programme in the inbox. The card's own decision 4 names the disciplined first slice: **one shared mailbox (forward/BCC-in), parsed and associated** covers most real demand at a fraction of per-user sync cost.

**Recommendation**: approve the direction and layering, but appetite-gate phase 1 to the shared-mailbox pattern + association seam + `sys_mail_message` only; per-user IMAP sync, CalDAV, and write-back become `Blocked-by:`-chained sub-issues after the seam proves out (contract-first split, one sub-issue per layer, spec-facing object shapes routed to the spec seat). The five design decisions need maintainer answers before any spec work starts.

Dependency flag: no open card carries a `Blocked-by:` pointing here today.

Triage: this comment comes from the triage seat Routine; not a claim.

**Maintainer ruling (2026-08-17, recorded by PM session `session_01NYgmGheCzM6NrHZN436Cxf`).** The maintainer held the dedicated design round on this card, approved the direction and all five design decisions per the PM analysis, and deliberately scheduled the work for v18. Verbatim: 「同意，请记录你的分析结论，但是这个任务我刻意标了 v18，暂时不做。」

This comment is the **design record** — written so the v18 implementer needs no chat context.

## Confirmed: direction, placement, architecture

- **Open-core placement confirmed.** Inbound mail is category table-stakes (every free-tier competitor ships it; email-to-record is the first thing every CRM evaluator tries), protocol plumbing not governance. The core/enterprise boundary stands as filed: *one person connecting their own IMAP mailbox is core; taking over 500 Exchange mailboxes at once is enterprise* (tenant-scale delegation, bulk provisioning, sync health = enterprise, filed separately).
- **Three-layer architecture confirmed**: connector (protocol + auth, `packages/connectors/` convention) / sync services (`service-mailbox`, `service-calendar` — separate engines, shared account+credentials) / **association seam** (the platform never learns what a "contact" is; one closed extension point — "given these participant addresses, which record(s)?" — answered by the app).
- **Phase 1 scope**: shared mailbox (forward/BCC ingest) + association seam + `sys_mail_message`, only. Per-user IMAP sync, CalDAV/calendar entirely, write-back, and the enterprise admin plane are all `Blocked-by:`-chained follow-ups. Calendar is deferred wholesale (bidirectional = harder, zero measured pull today).

## The five design decisions — ruled

**1. Mirror, not Adopt.** Platform owns faithful mirror objects (`sys_mail_message`, `sys_calendar_event`) whose schema is dictated by the external standards (RFC 5322 / iCalendar); apps keep their own business objects (`crm_event` etc.) linked by a declared association. Rationale on record: a mirror row and a business row carry **two different truths** ("what the external system says" vs "what the business recorded") — Adopt forces them into one object where sync semantics and business semantics collide (external deletion vs business retention; engine re-sync/dedupe vs app-written fields; every new app category renegotiating one shared shape). Mirror keeps sync mechanical and business free; it is `sys_email`'s proven shape, inbound. Under the AI-error axis it is decisive: Adopt invites AI authors to extend `sys_*` objects with business keys — the ungoverned platform-object-row surface #9054 measured; Mirror gives them a closed contract. Accepted costs: one indexed join on timelines; write-back (later) becomes an explicit opt-in projection rather than an accidental side effect.

**2. Association stamped at ingest + an explicit re-match action** — not read-time dynamic resolution. Timelines stay stable, attribution is a deterministic auditable fact (the compliance narrative of the regulated-market direction), and the RFI's 2s record-open budget survives. Contact-created-later / contact-changed cases are handled by the explicit re-match mechanism shared with decision 3 — state is declared, changes are recorded.

**3. Unmatched messages go to an unassociated pool, retro-matched when a contact is created** — never dropped (prospect-mails-first is the normal sales sequence). **Pool visibility defaults restricted** (mailbox admins/owners only, not org-wide) — the pool is the card's most privacy-sensitive corner.

**4. Shared mailbox first** — it *is* phase 1. The connector interface is designed now for the per-user shape (account + credential abstraction); phase 1 is its first implementor, so per-user later extends rather than rewrites.

**5. Privacy: "forwarding is consent" is phase 1's declared semantic.** The full declarable policy vocabulary (folder allowlist / participant-must-be-known-contact / per-message share) lands with the per-user phase, where the hard privacy surface actually lives — as **closed declarable keys, never runtime tolerance**. Design note pinned: the known-contact switch is semantically opposed to the unmatched pool (one rejects stranger mail, the other exists for it) — it must be an opt-in strictness knob, default OFF; the two must not both be defaults.

## Status: `pm:on-hold` — deliberately not now

- **Date**: 2026-08-17. **Reason**: the maintainer deliberately scheduled this at v18 (「刻意标了 v18，暂时不做」); nothing is dispatched and no sub-cards are carved yet.
- **Named restart condition**: the v18 planning window opens (v18 board work begins). On restart, this card becomes the **parent/coordination node** (never dispatched itself) and carves per the plan above: `connector-imap` · minimal `service-mailbox` (shared-mailbox ingest, parse, dedupe, attachments) · association seam + `sys_mail_message` (**spec accept-surface addition ⇒ spec seat, `claude-fable-5`**), plus `Blocked-by:` placeholder cards for per-user IMAP / CalDAV / write-back / enterprise admin plane.
- `target:v18` and `domain:services` stay.

Labels flipped `needs-user-decision` → `pm:on-hold` in the same stroke.

## Half-state patrol disposition (H9) — the hold gets a machine-fireable exit

`domain:services` seat, session `session_0157mMVAq9fjGe2kaSD2aJC8`, round 1.

Patrol anchor #9857 (swept 02:12:33Z) reports **H9** on this card: `pm:on-hold` with no `Restart-when:` line in either channel. Confirmed — body and thread both read, neither carries one. A hold with no fireable exit is a state nobody can lawfully leave, so this comment supplies the exit rather than leaving the card parked on nothing.

**Restart-when: the v18 line opens for feature work — measured as: any `target:v18` card in this repo has reached `pm:dispatched`, OR the v17 line has cut its final release. Then re-grade this card against the five open design decisions in its body (mirror-vs-adopt, association timing, unmatched pool, shared-vs-per-user mailboxes, privacy posture) before any dispatch.**

**Restart-touch: `packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/`, `packages/connectors/`** — an opportunistic restart fires if a dispatch's file surface intersects these and this card's premise is cheap to re-check while there.

### Why a hold and not the decision inbox

This card is **already carrying the maintainer's appetite answer in its labels**: `target:v18` says "yes, but on the v18 line". That is a decision already made, which is exactly what `pm:on-hold` means — as opposed to `needs-user-decision`, which means the decision is still owed. ⛔ So this one is **not** being escalated; it is being made lawfully parked. Two sibling cards in this sweep (#8103, #1883) did go to the inbox, because their decisions are genuinely unmade.

⚠️ Note for whoever picks it up: the five "Design decisions to settle" in the body **are** maintainer-floor questions (they shape a published platform object surface — `sys_mail_message`, `sys_calendar_event`). When the v18 line opens, this card wants a decision-box pass **before** it is dispatched, not a dispatch that decides them in a PR.

### Premise freshness

Body was verified against `0f539bd` on 2026-08-16. Re-check before acting:

```
git ls-tree -r --name-only origin/main packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/transports
git ls-tree --name-only origin/main packages/connectors/
git ls-tree --name-only origin/main packages/services/ | grep -i "calendar\|mailbox"
```
